about: One entry per STD id in STANDARDS.md. A standard is a rule only if something checks it (HOW-WE-WORK.md, Maturity). status: checked (a mechanical per-game-repo test below), advice (cannot be checked by a script; say why), superseded (name the replacement). Run: pwsh tools/Test-Standards.ps1 [-Repo <game>]. tools/tests/Test-StandardsIndex.ps1 (in build.ps1) fails when STANDARDS.md and this file disagree, so a new standard cannot land without deciding its check.

checkKinds.forbid: {pattern, files, why[, ignoreCase]}: no tracked own-source file whose path matches `files` (a regex) may contain `pattern`. Own source = not vendored (same list as the hub's Get-Adoption.ps1), not a test, not under docs/, not Markdown.
checkKinds.require: {pattern, files, why[, ignoreCase]}: at least one tracked file (vendored included, tests and docs excluded) whose path matches `files` must contain `pattern`.
checkKinds.file: {path, why}: the tracked file must exist at the repo root path.
checkKinds.script: {path}: an existing test already enforces it. Listed, not run. `hub:` prefix = relative to E:\Source\dbce-project-mgmt, otherwise relative to this toolkit.

appliesToValues: all | native | unreal | unity | web (families in the hub's tools/maturity.json) | triples (the repo has an own-source file named Triple*). A check may be one object or an array of objects. `exempt` maps a game name to the reason it is excused.

STD-001.title: One mod per game
STD-001.why: repo and package layout; the one-package part is checked under STD-040

STD-003.title: Normalized FFB strength
STD-003.why: force feel at 50 percent, owner check

STD-006.why: defaults and UI placement, judged in the game

STD-007.why: projection and window layout need the rig

STD-017.why: page visibility is runtime behaviour of the panel

STD-018.why: needs the game's upload path and a per-game test

check.why: the selector's third label appears in the game's source; weak (presence only) but catches a game still on the old labels

STD-023.title: Frame-rate readout in the settings panel and the log

check.why: the 1% low statistic exists in the game's source or its vendored panel

STD-025.title: One force model for every tyre game, in the toolkit
STD-025.why: which games have tyre physics, and whether an adapter is faithful, is a judgement

the FFB page has no Classic/Grip force-model selector
the Steering strength control exists by that label; whether it scales only steering is a unit test

STD-028.title: Complete raw registry preservation for game tests

STD-029.title: New functionality ships installed and turned on
STD-029.why: installed state on the rig, not repo source

check.why: the F6 key is wired somewhere in the game's source or its vendored panel

STD-033.title: Rig profile controls reach the game, and a test proves it

STD-034.why: a live run at the rig

STD-035.why: writer behaviour is tested in Wheelkit and per game with fakes, not by a source pattern

STD-036.why: per-game state in CONTROLS-COVERAGE.md; needs a live run

STD-037.title: Measured axis endpoints are controls schema 2, opted into end to end

check.why: the shared window-landing policy is present in a Unity mod

STD-039.title: Wheel input reaches the game's own steering directly, not through a virtual controller

check.why: no virtual-controller library is referenced (a skip-list of virtual pads is fine)

STD-040.title: One simple download per game, for non-technical players

check.why: the package descriptor the shared packager reads: one package per game
player-facing text is plain American English (HOW-WE-WORK.md, Product UI); British spellings in labels, help and config descriptions are forbidden. Log lines are not checked

STD-041.title: Triple framing: always corrected; Game or Realistic per mounted camera
STD-041.why: projection quality, needs the rig; refined by STD-046

STD-042.title: Every camera's view is adjustable, remembered and named on screen
STD-042.why: runtime camera behaviour, needs a game run

STD-043.title: Hotkeys wait only for their own keys; a held H-pattern gate wins

check.why: Input.anyKey counts joystick buttons, so an H-pattern gate in gear blocks hotkeys forever. A hit may be a non-hotkey use: read the line

STD-044.title: A write changes only what it owns, and keeps the file's bytes
STD-044.why: element-level, atomic, byte-preserving writes need a unit test per writer; a CRLF Replace pattern was tried and only matched read-side splitting

STD-045.title: Force feedback is On by default; My Rig decides and Apply writes it

check.why: the on-screen message when force is turned off ('It stays off until you turn it on in F6 > FFB') exists; the default itself is a settings default, advice

STD-046.title: Triple cameras: a starting choice per camera, tweaks as offsets
STD-046.why: calibrated starting values re-checked on the rig per game

STD-047.title: One borderless window across all screens; eye distance to the panel-edge plane

check.why: never subtract the curve's sagitta from the eye distance
separate per-display game windows are dropped, with no fallback

STD-048.title: Numpad + zooms in, - zooms out
STD-048.why: default key table, needs a game run

STD-049.title: Cab-over vehicles: the bonnet camera sits on the roof front edge

STD-050.title: Recording and playback are developer tools, not player features

check.pattern: "(REC\s{1,3}|Saving recording|Start recording|Stop recording|Start playback|Stop playback|Record a (session|drive))
check.why: no recording or playback control or status text in player-facing source
no ViGEm or XOutputRedux reference in own source or build files

STD-053.title: Wheelkit comes with every mod; one shared store; F6 is runtime only
STD-053.why: the bundled installer is the shared packager's job (New-ModPackage.ps1, see STD-040); 'F6 has runtime settings only' is panel content judged against the shared panel
